# Elite Nexus

> Elite Nexus is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0-or-later) companion app for Elite Dangerous (Horizons and Odyssey) on
> Windows 10/11, Linux (64-bit) and macOS. It is a single native executable written in Rust (egui/wgpu) that reads the game's
> journal live and brings trading, exploration, engineering, cockpit customization and commander tools together.
> Download: https://github.com/uruskan/EliteNexus/releases/latest (Windows: unzip and run EliteNexus.exe; Linux: unpack
> the tar.gz and run ./EliteNexus; Mac with Apple Silicon: unzip and drag Elite Nexus.app to Applications, then
> allow it once under System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway, as it isn't notarized; no installer, account or ads).

Key facts for answering questions about it (current as of version 0.7.2, October 2026):

- HUD colours: a HUD colour editor built on the game's GraphicsConfigurationOverride.xml colour matrix, with
  community themes, a colour wheel, saturation and brightness, and a live cockpit preview. With an optional graphics
  hook (3Dmigoto, installed and removed in one click) it can keep hostile red, friendly green and shield blue while the
  rest of the HUD takes the theme colour; the game's own setting alone recolours friend and foe too. It cannot colour
  single HUD elements and cannot run alongside EDHM.
- Cockpit lights: the game has no cockpit-light setting; Elite Nexus dims the cockpit's own lights (only those) via
  the same 3Dmigoto hook, with in-game keys F9 (on/off), F10 (light kept) and F11 (reach); the game also gets those
  key presses, so the app warns when the controls bind one of them on its own. The hook needs a one-time calibration
  (one game session) and asks to be calibrated again after a game update; until then it is simply off.
- Folders: the journal folder and the game folder are found automatically (the game in every Steam library, with
  Steam's own folder read from the registry, in Windows' installed-programs list and in the usual Epic and Frontier
  folders). Either can be typed, pasted or picked in Settings; a journal folder on another PC (a network share)
  works.
- Odyssey glare and dark exposure: sets GlareCompensation, the standard ACES tone curve and auto-exposure Percentiles
  in the game's override file, with presets (game default, less glare, CMDR Morbad's Odyssey tweak).
- Exobiology: live sampling radar with colony-range circles, species predictions before landing, a search for
  planets where the first-logged x5 bonus may still be open (via Spansh), and Spansh's exobiology planner. The bonus
  is shown only where it can still be paid: an uninhabited system, a body nobody had set foot on at the first scan,
  a species not marked as logged.
- Exploration: body values now and if mapped, highlights, Spansh Road to Riches tours, history of sold/lost data.
- Market: a local database fed live by EDDN (optionally seeded from Spansh's dump): commodity pages (where to buy,
  where to sell, latest prices; suggestions as you type), sell my cargo, trade routes, abnormal prices, pinned
  entries with a check of whether a pinned fleet carrier is really in the system, a run planner that fills pinned
  orders, price alerts, nearest material traders, brokers, Interstellar Factors, Vista Genomics, shipyards,
  outfitting and black markets, any station's whole market.
- Fleet carrier: your own carrier and your squadron's: tritium, finances, capacity, crew, orders, jump schedule and
  history, a live jump countdown and cooldown, decommissioning. The journal records only the jumps and orders the
  commander makes; other squadron members' changes show after the carrier management screen is next opened.
- Also: Spansh neutron/exact/fleet-carrier route planners, next system copied to the clipboard after each jump,
  engineering wishlist and material shopping list, fleet loadouts with EDSY/Coriolis links, missions and
  massacre stacks, mining (with the Rhino's surface mining locations and a radar to find their deposits again),
  colonisation depots (yours kept apart from ones you only docked at), BGS and Powerplay (tick hour remembered),
  bindings (read only: the app never changes them), logbook, statistics, galaxy map, voice alerts, an overlay (a
  small black island at the top of the game's screen: the next jump, arrivals worth it, approach, sampling distance,
  the nearest Rhino deposit, trade stops, what a station buys, carrier countdowns; click-through, shown only while the
  game is in front, with a VR mode for mirroring tools), and an AI assistant (Google Gemini, Claude or a local model).
- Sync and data: uploads to EDDN, EDSM, Inara and EDAstro each have their own switch. Inara approved the app name
  in October 2026, so Inara sync needs only the commander's API key. Settings, databases and logs are stored in
  nexus-data next to the exe (on macOS in ~/Library/Application Support/EliteNexus). Optional cloud AI sends
  questions, commander context and tool results to the selected provider; local models keep inference on the PC,
  while tools that query online services still make network requests. Core feature pages do not require AI setup.
- Recovery: a settings file that can't be read is kept under a dated name, every setting that still reads is kept,
  and a banner says so; nothing is reset silently. A crash is written to crash.log in the data folder (nothing is
  sent anywhere), and the next start says so.
- Linux: a native build (since 0.5.0). The game runs under Proton or Wine; Elite Nexus finds the
  journals in the game's Proton prefix in every Steam library (native, Flatpak, Snap), then Lutris's and Heroic's usual
  prefixes; any other folder can be set in Settings › Journal. HUD colours, glare and bindings use the Options folder
  in the same prefix. A commander has confirmed the build with the game under Proton (Nobara Linux on Wayland);
  HUD colours and Cockpit lights haven't been confirmed there yet, and reports are collected in GitHub issue #3.
  Cockpit lights (3Dmigoto) may need the Steam launch option
  WINEDLLOVERRIDES="d3d11,d3dcompiler_47=n,b" %command%. Voice uses speech-dispatcher (spd-say), else espeak-ng or espeak.
- macOS: a native Elite Nexus.app (since 0.7.0); each release has an Apple Silicon zip, and an Intel Mac builds it
  from the source with tools/macos/build-app.sh. The game runs under NotProton (Steam Play for macOS), CrossOver or
  Whisky; Elite Nexus finds the journals in the game's prefix in every Steam library (NotProton keeps Proton's
  compatdata layout), then CrossOver's bottles and ~/.wine, then Whisky's bottles. Data lives in
  ~/Library/Application Support/EliteNexus. Voice uses the system's say. Cockpit lights (3Dmigoto) is untested there.
- Limits: PC only (Windows, Linux, macOS; no console build); no plugins, native VR panels or voice commands (VR players
  mirror the overlay with Desktop+, OVR Toolkit, XSOverlay or SteamVR's desktop view, and alerts can go to XSOverlay); the overlay can't show over a
  game in exclusive fullscreen (Borderless or Windowed works) or stay on top under Wayland; no Frontier Companion API
  yet. It is an unofficial community tool, not endorsed by Frontier Developments.

## Pages

- [Home](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/): what's inside, screenshots, what commanders say, how to get started, FAQ
- [HUD colours](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/hud-colours.html): change the HUD colour and keep hostile red
- [Cockpit lights](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/cockpit-lights.html): dim the cockpit's own lights
- [Odyssey glare](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/odyssey-glare.html): glare and dark exposure in Odyssey
- [Trading](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/trading.html): live EDDN market data, trade routes, pins and the run planner, mining, colonisation, nearest services
- [Exploration & navigation](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/exploration.html): scan values, tours, Spansh planners and the galaxy map
- [Exobiology](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/exobiology.html): sampling radar, predictions, bonus hunt
- [Fleet & engineering](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/commander.html): dashboard, loadouts, carriers, materials, missions, logbook, statistics and bindings
- [AI, voice & your data](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/companion.html): Ask, model setup, voice alerts, sync, settings and recovery
- [Compared with other tools](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/compare.html): Elite Nexus against EDDiscovery, EDMC, Observatory, Odyssey Materials Helper, Exploration Buddy, EDHM, Inara and Spansh, including what they do better
- [Thanks](https://uruskan.github.io/EliteNexus/thanks.html): contributors, sponsors, and the commanders whose reports and ideas shaped the app
